author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Thousands of people gathered at London's Primrose Hill to watch a rare partial solar eclipse.
About 90 percent of the Sun was covered at the peak of the eclipse in London, creating a striking change in the sky.
For many younger spectators, it was their first experience of such an event, with the last eclipse of similar coverage in London occurring about 27 years ago.
Crowds watched as the sky darkened and temperatures dropped, turning the event into a shared experience in the heart of the capital.
One spectator described the eclipse as a special opportunity for the community to come together and witness a rare event.
The gathering at Primrose Hill drew people who arrived prepared to spend time watching the phenomenon, including with picnic blankets.
The eclipse provided a rare moment for thousands of Londoners to look up and experience the event together.

Al Jazeera's Sonia Gallego reports from London.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
This episode on the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda examines one of the few mass atrocities universally recognised under international law. It traces how colonial rule hardened fluid social categories into fixed Hutu and Tutsi identities, and how post-independence politics turned these into a racialised hierarchy of fear.

It also explores how economic crisis, civil war and the Arusha peace process created space for extremists, who used newspapers, churches and “hate radio” to prepare people for mass murder.

Through testimony and archive footage, the film follows how local officials, militias and neighbours organised killings at terrifying speed, and how international actors failed to intervene. It also looks into how courts, memorials and political power have since shaped Rwanda’s official narrative of the genocide.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The death toll from Monday's earthquake in Colombia has risen to more than 200 and is expected to increase as rescuers continue searching collapsed buildings.
Cali, one of the worst-hit areas, has seen volunteers and emergency teams work through the rubble in a desperate search for survivors.
At a collapsed apartment building, rescuers have yet to find anyone alive, although volunteers say they heard a man's voice beneath the debris.
A doctor was rescued alive from another collapsed building, raising hopes among families still waiting for news of loved ones.
At Cali's University Hospital, part of the building has collapsed, forcing patients to be evacuated as other medical facilities struggle to cope.
Families are facing uncertainty over the whereabouts of victims, with one father searching for his teenage son after being told he had died.
Officials say 30 percent of Cali's large and medium-sized medical centres are inoperative, further straining the emergency response.

title: Colombia earthquake death toll rises above 200 as rescuers race to find survivors

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Atif Najib, the former Syrian security chief in Daraa, has been sentenced to death for his role in the crackdown on protesters in 2011.
A criminal court in Damascus also handed down death sentences in absentia to eight other former regime figures, including Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher.
The defendants were convicted of war crimes, crimes against humanity, murder, arbitrary detention and torture, including of children.
The ruling is being seen as a landmark step towards transitional justice for victims of the Assad regime.
Families of those killed and detained in Daraa welcomed the verdict, with celebrations taking place outside the Palace of Justice in Damascus.
Najib's sentence cannot yet be carried out as legal appeals must first be completed, while Bashar and Maher remain in Russia.
The case is being closely watched as a test of whether Syria can turn judicial rulings into meaningful accountability.

Al Jazeera's Obaida Hitto reports from Damascus.

title: Syria sentences Bashar al-Assad and former officials to death over war crimes
